bench.note: Latency of torch.matmul only. Not a fused-kernel comparison. nsight_dram_bytes and achieved_ai are TBD.
bench.what_was_timed: torch.matmul or numpy matmul; not MemMode/ComputeMode kernels
bench.requested_peak_source: NVIDIA A40 datasheet, dense FP16 Tensor Core with FP16 accumulate 149.7 TFLOP/s (structural sparsity 299.4 unused), GDDR6 696 GB/s
bench.regime_label_note: regime_vs_h100_datasheet uses the H100 SXM FP16 datasheet ridge even when the GPU is not an H100. regime_vs_requested_datasheet uses --machine. Neither column is a measured ridge. achieved_ai is set only from Nsight DRAM bytes. proxy_ai from torch.profiler is allocator memory and is not achieved AI.

decision_agreement.note: quote_as_scic_accuracy is true only for isolated Nsight DRAM (status NSIGHT_DRAM). A process-sum Nsight capture and a torch profiler memory estimate still produce rates so the next run has a number to inspect; do not put those rates in the paper as SCIC accuracy. The ridge is still the datasheet ridge.

fusion_proxy.note: Proxy only. Two-kernel matmul+RMSNorm versus an eager chain and, when it runs, torch.compile. Bias+GELU compares two eager ops with one Python expression and, if importable, one Triton elementwise kernel. None of these is a fused GEMM, MemMode, ComputeMode, or Stage-Stream. Do not report the time ratio as a fusion speedup.
